scenario: Controlled ingestion queue backlog in the local Kubernetes lab
hypotheses: The queue-backlog anomaly was caused by an operator-enabled, bounded 30-second worker delay while 100 valid Markdown uploads were accepted with HTTP 202.
Removing the worker delay while keeping the worker replica available would drain the ARQ queue and clear the anomaly without changing queue names or retry behavior.
root_cause: A local, opt-in worker delay preserved the worker metrics endpoint but reduced ingestion throughput below the controlled upload rate. Prometheus recorded a pending state and then a firing InsightHubQueueBacklogAnomaly before the hook was removed.
mitigation: Deploy the same image with DAY4_CHAOS_ENABLED=false and DAY4_CHAOS_WORKER_DELAY_SECONDS=0; wait for the worker to drain the ARQ sorted-set queue and verify the alert clears.
evidence_interpretation: At 17:33:20 the recorded queue depth (70) was above the contemporaneous dynamic upper band (59.74); the rule was later observed firing after its hold period. Recovery samples show both recording and worker gauges at 1.
